title: Stretch the sensor to fill the ADC
story: A temperature sensor gives 0.5 V at 0 C and 1.0 V at 50 C, but the ADC spans 0 to 3.3 V. A difference amplifier subtracts a 0.5 V reference and multiplies by R2 / R1, with R1 = 10 kohm. The op-amp runs from 5 V, so it could swing above 3.3 V and harm the ADC. Pick the two R2 resistors (they must be equal) so that at 50 C, with the sensor at 1.0 V, the output sits between 2.9 V and 3.3 V: most of the range, without going over.

goals.label: output between 2.9 V and 3.3 V at 50 C

hints: With matched resistors, Vout = (R2 / R1) x (Vsensor - Vref).
At 50 C, Vsensor - Vref = 0.5 V, so you want R2 / R1 a little under 3.3 / 0.5 = 6.6.
If the two R2 resistors differ, the amplifier no longer subtracts cleanly and the output is wrong.
